label: GOD_NAMING senses: reference-fixed names are rigid, rigid node is the box node, readings separate
paraphrase: Premise-free comparison of the two naming senses. (1) For every model with worlds, existence and accessibility, descriptions D and D', reference world w0 and bearer x: a name reference-fixed at w0 by D is rigid (RigidAt) at every origin for the being x that alone, among the beings existing at w0, satisfies D at w0; at w0 the descriptive and the reference-fixed name designate the same bearers; and if x alone satisfies both D and D' at w0 among the beings existing there, the two reference-fixed names co-designate at every world accessible from w0 where x exists, and they co-designate at every accessible world iff x exists at every accessible world (necessity of identity, not necessary existence). (2) For every signature, profile and world, the GOD_NAMING_2 reading of the necessary-being node holds iff the box K node holds, and so does the GOD_NAMING_1 reading whose description is the route's world-independent GOD_4 predicate (both bridges hold trivially for it). (3) On explicit two-world models: the GOD_NAMING_1 node holds while the box K node and the no-other-possible-God bridge fail; the box K node and that bridge hold while the GOD_NAMING_1 node and the essential Godhood bridge fail; at a non-reference world the descriptive name designates a being and the reference-fixed name designates nothing; two descriptive names co-designate at the reference world and not at another world where their actual bearer exists, while the reference-fixed names co-designate there. (4) A model where both nodes and both bridges hold together.
